rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 3 (base_speed 1.0, sensors at x = ±0.04, kp 2.5, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, line_loss last_direction) scored 57.6, the best so far. Oval progress rose from 0.115 to 0.21, so speed was part of the cause. S-bend progress fell from 0.15 to 0.126 and slalom from 0.105 to 0.084, so slowing down did not solve the course in general. Every run still ended off track with exactly one line-loss event and max_error about 0.062 m, just above the 0.06 m limit. Oscillation stayed low (0.13 to 0.15), so the robot is not weaving. Gains, sensor span and speed have each been varied, and the line is still lost once per run. The failure therefore sits in the recovery after line loss, which Evaluator feedback identifies as the next suspect.

Change. I keep the iteration 3 geometry, base_speed 1.0, kp 2.5, ki 0.3, kd 0.1 and sensor weights unchanged, and change only controller.line_loss from last_direction to search_right. search_right holds the signal at +1, which steers the robot left. I chose this side arbitrarily, because the telemetry does not report which side max_error grows on. last_direction replays a fixed-sign turn of the last valid signal, and that turn is likely the wrong one or too weak to find the tape again. A single-variable change makes the effect of recovery mode clear.

Expected result. If the failure is recovery-limited, line_loss_events stays at 1 but the robot re-acquires the line, so progress should rise clearly above 0.21 on the oval and above 0.13 on the s-bend, and some runs should complete. If the robot instead leaves to the right, max_error will be larger on the right side, and the next step is search_left, which steers right. If progress does not change at all, recovery mode is not the limit, and the next test is lowering kp from 2.5 toward 2.0 to reduce bend-entry turn authority.

Hypotheses to check. H4: the line-loss recovery mode decides whether the robot re-acquires the line. H5: the failure side is the same on every track, so one search direction should be correct for all tracks. Next measurements: progress and line_loss_events per track, max_error per track, and completion_time if any run finishes.
